column2: In 1983, a computer told one man that five nuclear missiles were headed his way. And he decided to do nothing.
It's just after midnight in a secret bunker outside Moscow. Stanislav Petrov is watching a brand new satellite warning system.
Then the siren goes off. The screen says: one missile, launched from America. Then two. Then five.
His job is to report it. And a report like that could start a war.
But Petrov hesitates. His fear is telling him one story. The facts are telling him another.
You see, if America really attacked, it wouldn't send five missiles. It would send hundreds. And the ground radar? Nothing.
So he calls it a false alarm, and waits. One minute. Five. Nothing hits.
The satellite had mistaken sunlight bouncing off clouds for rocket engines.
Petrov's reward? A reprimand. For messy paperwork.
Sometimes the bravest thing you can do is question the first story your fear tells you.
